title: Design Patterns
description: The 23 classic Gang of Four object-oriented software design patterns.

results.name: Abstract Factory
results.description: Provides an interface for creating families of related objects without specifying their concrete classes.

results.name: Builder
results.description: Separates the construction of a complex object from its representation so the same process can create different representations.

results.name: Factory Method
results.description: Defines an interface for creating an object but lets subclasses decide which class to instantiate.

results.name: Prototype
results.description: Creates new objects by copying an existing prototypical instance rather than instantiating from scratch.

results.name: Singleton
results.description: Ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it.

results.name: Adapter
results.description: Converts the interface of a class into another interface clients expect, letting incompatible classes work together.

results.name: Bridge
results.description: Decouples an abstraction from its implementation so the two can vary independently.

results.name: Composite
results.description: Composes objects into tree structures to represent part-whole hierarchies, treating individual and composite objects uniformly.

results.name: Decorator
results.description: Attaches additional responsibilities to an object dynamically, providing a flexible alternative to subclassing.

results.name: Facade
results.description: Provides a unified, simplified interface to a set of interfaces in a subsystem.

results.name: Flyweight
results.description: Uses sharing to support large numbers of fine-grained objects efficiently by keeping common state extrinsic.

results.name: Proxy
results.description: Provides a surrogate or placeholder for another object to control access to it.

results.name: Chain of Responsibility
results.description: Passes a request along a chain of handlers until one of them handles it, decoupling sender from receiver.

results.name: Command
results.description: Encapsulates a request as an object, allowing parameterization, queuing, logging, and undoable operations.

results.name: Interpreter
results.description: Defines a grammar for a language and an interpreter that uses the representation to interpret sentences in it.

results.name: Iterator
results.description: Provides a way to access elements of a collection sequentially without exposing its underlying representation.

results.name: Mediator
results.description: Defines an object that encapsulates how a set of objects interact, promoting loose coupling.

results.name: Memento
results.description: Captures and externalizes an object's internal state so it can be restored later without violating encapsulation.

results.name: Observer
results.description: Defines a one-to-many dependency so that when one object changes state, all its dependents are notified automatically.

results.name: State
results.description: Allows an object to alter its behavior when its internal state changes, appearing to change its class.

results.name: Strategy
results.description: Defines a family of interchangeable algorithms and encapsulates each so they can vary independently of clients.

results.name: Template Method
results.description: Defines the skeleton of an algorithm in a method, deferring some steps to subclasses.

results.name: Visitor
results.description: Represents an operation to be performed on the elements of an object structure without changing their classes.
